extra.reason:
Fixed. Auto-backup now succeeds; bd invocations no longer print the warning.

ROOT CAUSE: the backup store held a manifest and no data. The manifest
referenced five table files -- cjrp1dd, gl8eeul, nf18v4q, p81gv35 and
tvj1uns -- and NONE existed on disk. The directory contained only
manifest, backup_state.json and a zero-byte LOCK. The error named just
one missing file per invocation, so it read as a single corrupt chunk
when in fact the entire backup was empty.

REPAIR: preserved the old manifest and backup_state.json to
/tmp/beads-backup-forensics/, confirmed by inventory that the store held
zero data files (so nothing could be lost by clearing it), removed the
stale manifest and state, re-initialised the destination, and ran
bd backup sync -- 8.9s, no error.

VERIFIED AFTER: the store now holds g2elf51...darc (5.2 MB) and
j7toqe7...darc (708 B), both referenced by the new manifest and both
present. bd stats runs clean with no warning.

SAFETY: the authoritative issue data was never at risk -- .beads/issues.jsonl
carries all 148 issues in HEAD and on origin/main, so the primary DB was
recoverable from git throughout regardless of the backup state.

RESIDUAL DEFECT, NOT FIXED HERE, UPSTREAM IN bd: `bd backup status` reports
"Database size: 0 B" both when the backup was genuinely empty and now that
it holds 5.2 MB. The one field that would let an operator notice an empty
backup is hardcoded-looking and cannot distinguish the two states. Anyone
relying on it will not be warned. Worth reporting upstream; the honest local
check is `du -sh .beads/backup` plus confirming the manifest's referenced
*.darc files exist.

WHY IT MATTERED: this checkout lost uncommitted work four times tonight,
and for 45 minutes the backup reported "Last backup: 44m ago" while holding
zero bytes. A backup that announces success and contains nothing is worse
than one that is visibly absent.

Fixed in c06071f. runOneWay now returns a SyncOutcome (copied | refused) instead of null; the refusal carries plan.warnings, bytesToCopy and destinationAvailable, and SyncRefused renders them. no-room states the shortfall. Severity stays off destructive since nothing ran. Note the issue's first acceptance line was slightly wrong: SyncPlanView already carried warnings (ipc.ts:1246) -- the loss was entirely in the component. typecheck passes, JS suite 107/107.

Fixed in c891127. manifest_of now emits NUL-terminated records, and move_verified compares with cmp on files rather than != on shell variables (a bash variable cannot hold a NUL). Measured on a two-file source containing a<newline>b.txt: before, 2 files produced 3 newline-terminated records; after, 2 records. Verified a ditto copy matches and a tree missing one file does not. This was a data-loss path, not a comment defect: the manifest match is what authorises rm -rf on the source. Documented what is NOT fixed: the ACL column comes from line-oriented ls -lde, so a newline in a name still bleeds into that field -- identically on both sides, so the entry is compared less specifically rather than wrongly.

Removed. 336 MB of stray build output at crates/rdirstat-core/src/target (someone had run with CARGO_TARGET_DIR pointed inside src/). Verified inert before deleting: nothing written in the preceding 6 hours, no process holding the path. After: 0 .rlib/.rmeta/.d files and 0 target/ directories anywhere under crates/, all 16 rdirstat-core source files intact, crates/rdirstat-core down to 412K. Nothing to commit -- the path was gitignored (.gitignore:4 target/), which is why it accumulated unnoticed.

Identified and fixed. The flaky test is devFixtures.test.ts:91 'hit-testing thousands of tiles is microseconds, so a quadtree is premature' -- a wall-clock assertion, perProbeUs < 500, that measured 842.7us on a 16-core host at load average 463. Fixed by raising the bound to 5000us with the reasoning recorded in the test: what it guards is an algorithmic regression (a linear scan no longer sufficing), which arrives as orders of magnitude, not a 1.7x wobble, so the old bound caught scheduler noise and little else. The measured number is logged unconditionally so drift stays visible. Corroboration for the bound: two subsequent clean runs logged 536.9us and 393.3us -- the first would have failed the old 500us bound, so the flake rate under load was far above the 1-in-6 originally observed. Functional assertions untouched. Suite is 111/111 across two consecutive runs. Note the issue's request for a reporter that names failures is still worth doing: I found this by reading an unpiped run, not from the CI-style output.
